stem:
Komal helps at home in two ways: she picks small stones out of uncooked rice before cooking, and she collects cream while churning milk for butter.

What is true about these separations?

options.text: Picking stones removes an unwanted part; churning collects a useful part.
Both actions only remove unwanted parts, so collecting cream is not a separation goal.
Both actions look like stirring food, so they are not real separations.
Picking stones collects a useful part, and churning removes an unwanted part.

teacher.key_rationale: Handpicking stones removes unwanted material; churning gathers useful cream/butter. Separations can serve either purpose; stirring alone is not the criterion.
